meta.title: Fenix A320 Flow
meta.scope: Persönliche Simulator-Hilfe für den Fenix A320 in MSFS 2024 – kein Airline-SOP, nicht für den echten Flugbetrieb.
meta.basis: V2 (Astra) mit stabilen IDs, Inhalt ursprünglich aus V1 (Fable) und deinem Flow von 2024.

FCOM.label: FCOM
FCOM.text: Airbus Flight Crew Operating Manual – Inhalt nach der Verfahrensquelle bzw. Airbus-Standard, nicht Zeile für Zeile gegen ein FCOM des CFM-Sharklet-Musters geprüft.

FCTM.label: FCTM
FCTM.text: Airbus Flight Crew Techniques Manual – empfohlene Technik, nach Airbus-Standard zusammengefasst.

NCL.label: NCL
NCL.text: Airbus Normal Checklist – Aufbau mit Strich (down to the line / below the line).

QRH.label: QRH
QRH.text: Vorliegendes QRH (EC-MLE, A320-232/IAE, März 2016) – nur für Wortlaut und Bedingungen, nicht für Leistungswerte.

PROC.label: PROC
PROC.text: A320 Normal Procedures (TheAirlinePilots) – betreiberlastige, FCOM-basierte Zusammenstellung; Hauptquelle von V1.

SIM.label: SIM
SIM.text: Simulator-Trainingsblätter (u. a. FSLabs) – nur für die Simulation, Übertragbarkeit auf den Fenix nicht belegt.

FENIX.label: FENIX
FENIX.text: Fenix-/MSFS-spezifische Bedienung – kein Verfahren des echten Flugzeugs.

TECH.label: TECHNIK
TECH.text: Für die Weltreise zusammengefasste Technik (V3) – aus den Verfahren oben abgeleitet; Leistung immer aus dem EFB.

phases.title: Prelim Prep — Setup & Power
phases.note: First flow of the day. Only the **Weather Radar** items are repeated on transit checks. Battery voltage is checked with the BAT pushbuttons **OFF**.

items.detail: Your world-tour aircraft: Fenix A320 CEO with CFM56-5B engines and sharklets. Confirm variant, livery, payload and fuel in the Fenix EFB before powering up.
The full flow starts from a cold and dark cockpit. If you load a later panel state, mark the power-up steps that are already done as N/A.
Radar OFF on the pedestal panel before applying power. This is the only prelim-prep item repeated during transit checks.
Collins WXR-1200 baseline. Honeywell RDR-4000 units differ — check which radar the airframe has.

items.caution: Check voltage with the BAT pushbuttons **OFF** — not ON. Your original flow read the voltage without this step.
items.detail: >25.5 V confirms a charge above 50%. At or below 25.5 V: charge 20 min with BAT pb AUTO + EXT PWR ON, then re-check. Verify the battery contactor closes on the ELEC page.
The A320 BAT pushbutton has AUTO (pressed in) and OFF (released) — there is no "ON" position. Your original flow said "ON"; the correct callout is AUTO.
Press EXT PWR when the AVAIL light is lit. If the aircraft was electrically supplied within the last 6 h, the voltage check above can be skipped.
BAT pb OFF then ON to start a charging cycle. After 10 s the charging current should be < 60 A and decreasing. If not, repeat the check after the cycle ends.

items.caution: If the APU will be started on batteries, start it within 30 min of selecting BAT to AUTO. Beyond ~35 min the charge can fall below 25%.

items.detail: Carried over from your flow. Set the communication frequencies and select the audio channels you want to monitor.

items.caution: Holding the APU FIRE test pb **longer than 3 seconds** can auto-shut down the APU **and discharge the fire bottle**. Press briefly.
items.detail: The APU fire pb is only partially lit when AC power is unavailable — that is normal, not a fault.
Wait 3 s after the master switch before pressing START. Keep external power connected to reduce APU load, especially in hot weather.

items.caution: Do **not** use APU bleed while an LP or HP ground air unit is connected — check the BLEED page for existing pressure first.
items.detail: Your original flow waited 3 min after APU AVAIL before selecting bleed. The source procedure has no such delay: bleed is selected as required once the APU is available. The real constraint is the ground-air unit, not a timer.

phases.title: Prelim Prep — ADIRS & Acceptance
phases.note: IRS alignment takes ~10 min. Start it early so it runs while you do the rest of the preparation.

items.detail: A complete alignment is required: before the first flight of the day · after a crew change · departure airport between 2°N and 2°S · GPS unavailable with poor NAVAID coverage en route · GPS unavailable and flight time over 3 h. Your original flow had no alignment criteria at all.
If a complete alignment is not required but the IRS-to-FMGC position difference is 5 NM or more (POSITION MONITOR page), perform a fast alignment.
Recalls all cleared and cancelled warnings so nothing hidden is carried into the flight.
In the Fenix EFB, check the aircraft configuration and any simulated failures before planning performance.
Confirm the INOP SYS list is compatible with the MEL.

In icing conditions with OAT +3 °C or below, check the previous flight's taxi-in time to work out the remaining taxi-out time before the next engine acceleration for ice shedding (FCOM PRO-NOR-SUP-ADVWXR).
Check computerised fuel figures for gross errors, and that "last flight FOB + uplift = current FOB".

Load the planned payload and fuel in the Fenix EFB. Use the final loadsheet: MACZFW is ZFWCG; MACTOW is takeoff CG. Check that the aircraft has finished loading. Never substitute a default CG when the actual value is missing.
Compare OPT and CONF 2 performance. If the TFLEX difference is under 3 °C, take the higher flap setting. Short or poorly paved runway → higher flaps. Better climb gradient → lower flaps.

phases.title: Before Walkaround
phases.note: Split into a seated part (systems on the ECAM SD pages) and a standing part (equipment and circuit breakers). The alternate-brake check is done before the first flight of the day only.

items.detail: Source procedure (CFM56): minimum 9.5 qt plus an estimated consumption of about 0.5 qt per flight hour — for a 2-hour leg that is 10.5 qt. Not verified against a CFM56-5B FCOM; treat it as a planning value.
Fluid volume changes with OAT and can read out of range without any low-level or low-pressure warning. Contact maintenance if it does.

If the value is half-boxed amber, refer to FCOM LIM-OXY for minimum flight-crew oxygen pressure — it varies with crew number and temperature. Your original flow used a fixed >1000 psi; the real minimum comes from the table.

items.caution: If a flight-control surface disagrees with its handle position, contact maintenance **before** applying hydraulic power.

items.detail: Use the yellow electric pump to recharge if required.
The parking brake must be ON for the exterior inspection so the brake wear indicators can be read. With one brake above 500 °C (350 °C with brake fans on), avoid the parking brake unless necessary.

Yellow elec pump OFF · chocks ON · parking brake OFF · press pedals and read the triple indicator · release pedals · parking brake ON. Pressure must build symmetrically without delay; at full pedal deflection it must read between 2000 and 2700 psi.

Life jackets · smoke hoods · gloves · axe · portable fire extinguisher · oxygen masks (goggles attached) · escape ropes. Memory aid: put on the life jacket and smoke hood, pull on the gloves, take the axe in one hand and the extinguisher in the other, use the rope to get out and breathe fresh oxygen.
Overhead (49 VU) and rear panels (121, 122, 123, 124, 125 VU).

phases.title: Cockpit Prep — Overhead
phases.note: Worked left to right across the overhead panel, following zone 1 of the flow pattern. Both pilots cover their own side.

items.caution: Tell any ground crew on the intercom first — the test produces a **loud noise** in their headset.
items.detail: After testing, check there is no REGUL LO PR message on the DOOR/OXY page. Residual pressure between the LP valve and the masks can mask a closed-failed LP valve; absence of REGUL LO PR is what confirms the valve is open.
After refuelling is complete.
Check the CAB PRESS page actually displays LDG ELEV AUTO.

FCOM: LO only with few occupants (fewer than 141 on the A320), HI for abnormally hot and humid conditions. With a normal passenger load NORM is right. Your 2024 flow simply set the temperature knobs to 12 o'clock.
After refuelling is complete.

If the centre tank holds under 200 kg for the flight and FUEL CTR TK PUMPS LO PR cautions appear, set FUEL MODE SEL to MAN and CTR TK PUMPS OFF. Leaving MODE SEL in MAN on the ground with the pumps not OFF risks fuel spillage.
Check both the ECAM warning and the master switch lights.
Annunciator light test — confirms no failed indicator lamps before departure.
Set QNH on both sides. Note the readings on the flight plan.
Maximum allowed differences: PFD to PFD 20 ft · PFD to field elevation 75 ft (RVSM tolerance) · PFD to ISIS 100 ft.
Use of the ISIS bugs function is not recommended.
From the departure clearance and chart — e.g. 5000 ft or FL070. This is independent of the PERF thrust-reduction and acceleration altitudes.

items.caution: Do not engage autothrust on the ground — it can trigger AUTO FLT A/THR OFF at engine start.

items.detail: If the date is wrong, set it manually and leave the mode on INT for the whole flight. Date initialisation must finish in under a minute or the CFDS needs a maintenance reset to re-sync the lower ECAM time. Sync with GPS at least once a day.
Setting the third ACP PA knob to RECEPT lets the CVR record cabin announcements. Keep the volume above the medium range. Your original flow pulled the PA switch without this detail.
Set the code from the clearance. Without an assigned code the ICAO default is 2000; VFR uses 7000 in Europe and 1200 in the USA.

phases.title: FMS Prep — INIT & F-PLN
phases.note: Insert the **weights last** — entering them earlier forces repeated prediction computations. To find the right VIA, check on the second MCDU where the STAR ends.

items.detail: Selecting the secondary nav database on the A/C STATUS page deletes the whole flight plan — useful for a clean start.
As stated on the flight plan.
Check the tropopause value is accurate — it drives FMS prediction accuracy.
Walk the plan against the charts with constraints displayed.
e.g. EDDM26R — gives a live bearing and distance reference.
On the POSITION MONITOR page each IRS should be under 5 NM from the FMS position. Confirm the aircraft position on the ND against the airport, SID and surrounding navaids.

phases.title: FMS Prep — PERF & Engine-Out
phases.note: The engine-out setup below is an **operator technique**, not a generic Airbus procedure — it is kept because it is genuinely useful, but marked **§** so you know where it comes from.

items.detail: Insert the weights after all other entries to avoid repeated prediction cycles.

The FMS proposes a default (usually 1500 ft above the airport). Replace it with the values of the departure or noise-abatement procedure. The PERF fields are altitudes (ft QNH), not heights above the aerodrome.
A green-dot discrepancy between the FMGS and the takeoff performance application means the two are using different takeoff weights. Resolve it before departure.
Sets up the takeoff-alternate or immediate-return option without disturbing the active plan.
e.g. MUCX4. Place it as the 2nd waypoint after the departure airport.
e.g. EDDM26R — draws the extended runway track on the ND.
Check the engine-out SID routing and constraints against the chart — this is what the setup above supports.
Engine-out acceleration altitude from the takeoff performance. Brief it together with the maximum acceleration altitude (TOGA time limit).

phases.title: Briefings
phases.note: Keep it interactive and in logical sequence. The goal is a shared game plan: identify the threats, identify deviations from routine, agree on how to mitigate both.

items.detail: DATA page: type and model, APD and nav database validity.
Runway, takeoff config, FLEX or TOGA, V-speeds, transition altitude, thrust reduction and acceleration altitude.
Length, width, stopway, surface condition, lighting. Also packs and anti-ice for takeoff.
Noise abatement, weather, terrain, failure contingencies (communication, technical), EO SID and other contingencies.

Call out the malfunction clearly; PF calls STOP or GO. On STOP: apply the rejected-takeoff procedure, bring the aircraft to a complete stop, set the parking brake and call "ATTENTION CREW AT STATION". PM monitors REV GREEN and DECEL, silences aural warnings, informs ATC. ECAM actions on command. Evacuate via the Emergency Evacuation checklist if required.

Continue. No action below 400 ft AGL except gear up and silencing warnings; then ECAM actions on command. Level off at the engine-out acceleration altitude once the engine is secured — at the latest at the maximum acceleration altitude (TOGA time limit). Accelerate, clean up, green dot, MCT; then ECAM, status, relight; follow the EO routing or an immediate return.

phases.title: Before Pushback & Start
phases.note: A quick look at the E/WD memo before push catches the classics: PARK BRK · NW STRG DISC · TCAS · APU (reminder to disconnect GPU and AC van).

items.detail: If actual ZFW exceeds estimated ZFW by 2000 kg a new flight plan is required. Fuel discrepancy tolerance: 400 kg up to 6 t uplift, 500 kg between 6 and 12 t, 600 kg above 12 t.
From both ATC and ground. Confirm the ground crew is ready and pass them the start sequence.

items.caution: Deselect EXT PWR **before** the ground engineer disconnects it — disconnecting with the pb still ON may cause injury.

items.detail: For the sliding window check the red indicator on its handle; for doors and slides use the lower ECAM DOOR page.
"Cabin crew prepare for departure, arm the door slides and cross check."

items.caution: If the memo is **not** displayed but the ground crew confirms the bypass pin is in the towing position, do **not** start engines during pushback — green hydraulic pressurisation could damage the nose gear.

items.detail: Release when the ground crew asks. Note the off-blocks time and start the clock.

phases.title: Engine Start
phases.note: **Engine 2 is started first** — it drives the yellow hydraulic system, which pressurises the parking brake. Automatic start is the norm; manual start is a read-and-do supplementary procedure.

items.caution: Engines start regardless of lever position, but thrust rises rapidly to whatever the levers command. Confirm IDLE.

items.detail: Engine 2 first: it powers the yellow hydraulic system that pressurises the parking brake. Select ON only once all amber crosses and messages have cleared from the engine parameters and bleed pressure is available.
N2 increases, start valve in line, bleed pressure green, oil pressure rising.
CFM56 auto-start: igniter at about 16% N2, fuel at about 22% N2, start valve closes at about 50% N2.
Fuel flow may cross approximately 200 kg/h.

items.caution: EGT and N1 must increase within 15 s (max) after fuel is on. If not, abort the start.

items.detail: Start valve closure begins and the igniter indication goes out.
Approximate ISA sea-level CFM56 values for recognition, not hard limits: N1 20%, N2 60%, EGT 400 °C, FF 300 kg/h. Confirm normal indications for the actual conditions.
Same sequence as engine 2. PTU FAULT is triggered if the last engine is started within 40 s of cargo-door operation ending — reset by cycling the yellow ELEC pump ON then OFF.
Both packs reopen with a 30 s delay after the second engine passes N2 50%.

phases.title: After Start
phases.note: After start, run the engines at or near idle for at least **2 minutes** before advancing to high power — taxi time at idle counts toward this.

items.detail: This is the cue to begin the after-start flow.
Avoids ingesting engine exhaust gases. If the APU is needed for performance, bleed may be selected ON again before takeoff.

Must be ON for all ground operations when icing conditions exist or are anticipated — OAT/TAT below 10 °C with visible moisture. In icing with OAT +3 °C or below, carry out the ice-shedding procedure.

items.caution: APU bleed is **not authorised** for wing anti-ice.
items.detail: Turn on if there is evidence of ice accretion — ice on the visual indicator or wipers, or a SEVERE ICE DETECTED alert. Accretion is severe at roughly 5 mm or more.
If no longer required.

items.caution: In icing conditions with rain, slush or snow, keep flaps **retracted** until the takeoff point.

items.detail: If the status reminder is displayed, review the ECAM status page.
Then: "hand signal on the left/right". After the signal, call "HAND SIGNAL RECEIVED AND BYPASS PIN SIGHTED".

phases.title: Taxi
phases.note: FCTM technique: on long straight taxiways let the aircraft accelerate to about **30 kt**, then one smooth brake application down to about **10 kt** — fewer, firmer applications save the carbon brakes. Below 10 kt for turns of 90° or more. Local and low-visibility limits always apply.

items.detail: Full deflection on both sidesticks and rudder, watching the F/CTL page. May be done before or during taxi.
Slight residual pressure may show briefly.
Call "BRAKE CHECK" / "PRESSURE ZERO" — no pressure on the triple gauge. After long parking in the wet, the first application at low speed is less effective.
F-PLN (SID, transition), initial climb speed and speed limit, FCU cleared altitude, HDG preset, FD both ON, PFD/ND check.
Consider radar on the PF side and terrain on the PM side.
Select IGN for heavy rain, standing water on the runway, or if severe turbulence is expected after takeoff.
Airbus has one Before Takeoff checklist: the part down to the line during taxi, the rest at line-up.

items.caution: Brake fans must be **OFF** for takeoff. Fans-off brake temperature limit for takeoff is **300 °C**.
items.detail: If an arc shows on the WHEEL page above brake temp, set fans ON. The sensor cools faster than the brake itself, so switching fans OFF will show a temperature rise — select fans OFF if the temperature with fans on is below 150 °C, otherwise delay takeoff.

items.caution: Double-check runway direction after line-up using the localizer, ND and runway markings.

items.detail: Visually and via TCAS.
Consider packs OFF, or APU bleed ON provided wing anti-ice is OFF. Packs OFF improves performance with TOGA and reduces takeoff EGT (and maintenance cost) on a FLEX takeoff.
"Cabin crew take your stations for takeoff."

phases.title: Takeoff
phases.note: Captain keeps a hand on the thrust levers until V1. The takeoff-roll technique follows your flight profile: standard, or strong crosswind above 20 kt / tailwind.

items.detail: Also check weather and terrain around the departure path, and the fuel state before takeoff.
Let the engines stabilise before advancing.
Half forward up to 80 kt, progressively neutral by 100 kt. Counters the nose-up effect of setting takeoff thrust.
Let the engines stabilise at 50% before the further increase.
Rapidly increase to 70% (1.15 EPR), then progressively to takeoff thrust by 40 kt ground speed.
MAN TOGA or MAN FLX, SRS, RWY (or blank), A/THR in blue.
Below 80 kt an EGT overlimit triggers ECAM and the takeoff can be rejected. Above 80 kt it is inhibited — EGT may exceed red line but do not reject above 100 kt.
Rotate smoothly at about 3°/s toward 15° pitch, then follow SRS.
The AP can be engaged from 100 ft AGL and at least 5 s after liftoff. Follow SRS until then.

phases.title: After Takeoff & Climb
phases.note: Flow first, then the **AFTER TAKEOFF / CLIMB** checklist: down to the line once the flaps are up and the packs are on, below the line at the transition altitude.

items.detail: Set pack 2 ON about 10 s after pack 1 for passenger comfort. Packs ON before reducing thrust will increase EGT.
At F speed with a positive speed trend, retract to CONF 1. Note: in CONF 1+F the F speed does not appear on the PFD. Your original flow collapsed both retraction steps into one "above S speed" item.

items.caution: Slat alpha/speed lock inhibits retraction from 1 to 0 if AOA exceeds 8.5° or speed drops below 148 kt. It clears below 7.6° AOA and above 154 kt.
items.detail: In CONF 1+F the flaps also retract automatically to 0 when IAS exceeds 210 kt, with the slats staying out.
Engine anti-ice ON when icing conditions exist or are anticipated, except in climb and cruise when SAT is below −40 °C.
Set STD at the transition altitude and cross-check both sides.
Baro reference STD, cross-checked on both sides.
EFIS CSTR/ARPT · landing lights retract · seat belts as required · ECAM memo and pressurisation review · clear manually tuned VORs · SEC F-PLN copy active · check OPT/MAX ALT.
At 10 000 ft or the highest MSA, whichever is later.
Approaching the assigned level, keep the vertical rate below 1500 fpm through the last 1000 ft (ideally 500–1000 fpm) to avoid unnecessary TCAS RAs.

phases.title: Cruise
phases.note: Mnemonic **A–I**. Green dot below 20 000 ft ≈ (2 × weight in tonnes) + 85; add 1 kt per 1000 ft above that.

items.detail: RVSM requirement.
Review suitable alternates, terrain, weather, fuel and the applicable engine-out performance. A fixed 350 NM does not define single-engine range without fuel, time, mass and flight conditions.

At the same waypoint compare actual FOB and fuel used with the OFP/SimBrief plan. Check FOB + total fuel used against the initial fuel quantity, using the applicable tolerances. Review destination/alternate predictions separately. A future-waypoint prediction must not be compared directly with the present tank quantity.
A range of 80 NM on the PF ND and 160 NM on the PM ND is a good combination.
Update when wind differs by 30° or 30 kt, or temperature deviation by 5 °C. Your original flow requested winds on a 6-hourly clock; the source ties it to actual deviation.
Up: step flight level. Down (if FMGS fails): green dot speed and single-engine ceiling. Lateral: waypoint track and distance, NAV accuracy.
Fuel cools toward TAT at roughly 3 °C/h (up to 12 °C/h in extremes). Below the tropopause a 4000 ft descent gives about 7 °C more TAT; M +0.01 gives about 0.7 °C. Allow up to an hour to stabilise.

phases.title: Descent Prep & Arrival Briefing
phases.note: Obtain destination and alternate weather about **15 min before TOD**. Landing weight = GW − (FOB − estimated fuel at destination).

items.detail: Best combination to save fuel and brake wear: CONF 3 + REV idle + autobrake LO. If landing distance is the priority: CONF FULL + REV max + autobrake MED.
LO for long runways, MED for short or contaminated. Pedal braking may suit very long runways, or very short ones where full manual braking without delay is wanted.
The FMS may delete altitude constraints at or above the cruise level. If TOO STEEP PATH shows after the final descent point, do not use FINAL APP guidance.
Compare the F-PLN from the final approach fix to the missed approach point with the chart: track, altitude constraints and final descent angle. Do not modify the final approach segment.

Insert the tower wind without gusts — ground-speed mini already covers them. Minimum: the barometric minimum (DA for ILS CAT I, MDA or DA for non-precision) goes into the MDA field; the DH field is only for CAT II/III radio minima.
Including terminal information, NOTAMs and extra holding fuel.
Cycling the seat-belt sign twice just before TOD cues the cabin crew for descent.

phases.title: Descent
phases.note: Max rate of descent: **2000 fpm** below 5000 ft AGL and **1000 fpm** below 2000 ft AGL. Approaching the assigned level, reduce to 1000 fpm or less.

items.detail: If not managed: 0.78 / 300 kt down to FL100, then 250 kt below FL100.
Select at 10 000 ft or MSA, whichever is higher. If NAV accuracy is LOW, do not use TERR ON ND.
EFIS CSTR · LS as required · NAV accuracy check · landing lights set · seat belts ON · RAD NAV selected and identified · engine mode as required.
Your flow used "15 min before landing or below FL150". The source ties it to the 10 000 ft checks, which is the standard trigger.
IGN for standing water on the runway or heavy rain.
Approaching TL and when cleared to an altitude.
Visible moisture with TAT at or below 10 °C.

phases.title: Approach
phases.note: **ILS and RNAV (FINAL APP):** decelerated approach — CONF 1 and S speed at the final descent point, landing configuration and VAPP by 1000 ft. **Selected non-precision (TRK/FPA):** early stabilised — landing configuration and VAPP before the final descent point. Never forget: speed control · approach mode · configuration points · go-around altitude.

items.detail: Activates automatically when overflying the DECEL pseudo-waypoint in NAV mode. In HDG mode activate manually on PERF DES, about 15–20 NM from touchdown.
NAV ACCURACY HIGH on the PROG page. If it is LOW, at least one ND must show ROSE LS or VOR raw data.
Arm when cleared for the approach and on an intercept heading or track. FMA: LOC and G/S blue.

items.state: AS RQRD — BOTH FOR CAT II/III
items.detail: One AP is enough for a CAT I approach. Autoland and CAT II/III need both APs (CAT 2 / CAT 3 DUAL on the FMA).
Capture from below is the normal case. For a capture from above use the special card “G/S Interception from Above”.
An RNAV (GNSS) approach needs GPS PRIMARY. If GPS PRIMARY is lost before the final descent point, do not continue the RNAV approach unless visual.
Press when cleared and established on — or in NAV towards — the final approach track. FMA: APP NAV green, FINAL blue.
The vertical-deviation scale on the PFD shows the aircraft relative to the final descent path.
At the final descent point the FMA changes to FINAL APP (green) and the descent starts.
Once FINAL APP is engaged and the descent has started, set the missed-approach altitude.
Early stabilised: gear down, landing flaps, ground spoilers armed and VAPP before the final descent point, so the descent starts fully configured.
Fly the final track with TRK; the bird on the PFD shows the flight path.
Preset the charted final descent angle and pull it about 0.2 NM before the final descent point so the aircraft joins the path.
Once established in the final descent, set the missed-approach altitude.
Compare the altitude with the chart's distance table and correct the FPA in small steps (0.1–0.5°).
"Cabin crew at your stations for landing."

Select flaps 1 at least 3 NM before the final descent point. Establish on final descent with flaps 1 and S speed at or above 2000 ft AGL. If tailwind exceeds 20 kt or the glide is steeper than 3.5°, use an early stabilised approach instead.
After glide-slope capture, set the missed-approach altitude and cross-check it.
If intercepting below 2000 ft AGL, take flaps 2 at one dot below the flight path. Speed brakes are not recommended below 2000 ft.

Confirm down-and-locked indications for nose, left main and right main gear. On the WHEEL page this means at least one green triangle for each gear, with the applicable landing-gear memo. Check the brake triple indicator for residual pressure.
Retract speed brakes before selecting full flaps. To minimise flap wear, extend at VFE−15 where possible.
Retain CONF 3 and confirm VAPP from the landing performance.
ON when ice accretion is evident — ice on the visual indicator or the wipers. With significant ice on the airframe apply the icing corrections of the landing performance.

items.caution: Stabilised by **1000 ft** above the airport (500 ft for a visual approach in VMC). Not stabilised → go around.
items.detail: Criteria: speed +10/−5 kt · pitch +10°/−2.5° · bank 7° · sink rate max 1000 fpm · LOC and glide within ½ dot · hands on thrust levers and sidestick · briefings and checklists complete. The source procedure uses 1500 ft for CAT II/III. With more than 10 kt tailwind at landing it does not permit a decelerated approach.
Non-precision: treat the MDA (plus an add-on, often 50 ft) as a decision altitude — no level-off at MDA (continuous descent final approach).

A320 minimum AP use heights: ILS with CAT 1 on the FMA 160 ft AGL · FINAL APP, V/S or FPA 250 ft AGL · after a manual go-around 100 ft. Autoland follows the CAT II/III procedure. Your 2024 flow used 300 ft — a stricter personal policy, fine to keep.

phases.title: Landing
phases.note: Flare at about **30 ft**. "RETARD" sounds at 20 ft as a reminder — thrust levers must be at IDLE by touchdown at the latest, or the ground spoilers are inhibited.

items.detail: Typical pitch increment in the flare is about 4°, giving roughly −1° flight path angle with a 10 kt speed decay. Do not allow the aircraft to float. Your original flow noted 1°, which understates it.

items.caution: Ground spoilers are **inhibited** if the thrust levers are not at IDLE by touchdown.
Tailstrike above 13.5° pitch (11.5° with gear compressed). Wingtip or engine scrape above 20° roll (16° compressed).
items.detail: PM calls "PITCH, PITCH" at 10° and "BANK, BANK" at 7°.
Do not attempt a landing immediately after a high bounce — thrust may be needed to soften the second touchdown and the remaining runway may be insufficient.
If no spoilers: verify both levers at idle or reverse, set max reverse and press the brake pedals fully. If spoilers were not armed, selecting reverse will extend them.

items.caution: Autobrake does not activate if the ground spoilers have not activated.

items.detail: On snow-covered surfaces stow at 25 kt. For an autoland, stow at the end of the roll-out together with disconnecting the autopilot. Do not move the levers beyond forward idle.

phases.title: After Landing
phases.note: Ground spoilers disarming is the cue to start the flow. Complete the cleanup only once clear of the runway.

items.detail: Strobe AUTO after vacating. Landing lights retract, others as required.

Cold weather: flaps 0 unless the approach was in icing conditions or the runway is contaminated — ground crew must then check for obstructing ice first. Hot weather: keep slats in CONF 1 when OAT is above 30 °C to avoid AIR L(R) WING LEAK warnings. On terminating flights retract fully to 0 for the securing checklist.
Delay as long as possible. Use one pack if possible and alternate packs between flights to spread the wear.

Delay brake fans at least 5 min after landing, or until before stopping at the gate. Use them sooner if turnaround is short or temperature is likely to exceed 500 °C. Maintenance action is due if one brake exceeds 900 °C, or the difference between two brakes on a gear exceeds 150 °C with one at or above 600 °C.
Your technique: shut down engine 2 about 2 min after vacating, or 3 min after high thrust. Switch the electric hydraulic pump ON. This matches the FCOM 3-minute cooldown rule below.

phases.title: Parking & Securing
phases.note: Engine masters OFF **no less than 3 minutes** after high-thrust operation. Mnemonic for performance monitoring: **I-F-E** — IRS, Fuel, ECAM.

items.detail: If pressure is low, chocks are required before engine 1 shutdown.
Just before engine shutdown, to avoid exhaust fumes entering the cabin. If the APU is unavailable, use external power.

items.caution: No less than **3 minutes** after high-thrust operation. Check engine parameters decreasing.

items.detail: After confirming all engines have spooled down. Your original flow used "N2 below 20%" — spool-down is the actual condition.
"Cabin crew prepare for arrival, disarm door slides and cross check."

Release after chocks are on if one brake exceeds 300 °C (150 °C with fans). Do not press the pedals before releasing — that activates the zero-torque pressure function. Keep it on with a flat nose tyre to avoid yawing at release.
On POSITION MONITOR read each IRS deviation from the FMGC position against the FCOM PRO-NOR-SOP-22 limits.
An unusual discrepancy means maintenance action. Allow 5 min after shutdown for the gauges to settle.
Keeping it on reduces the hydraulic leak rate.

items.caution: Slats and flaps must be retracted **before** all ADIRS are set OFF simultaneously, or the rudder travel limit unit mechanical stop can be damaged.

items.detail: After ADIRS shutdown, wait 10 s before electrical shutdown so the units can memorise the most recent data.
If electrical power is needed for servicing, set the overhead MAINT BUS switch ON before removing aircraft power.

items.caution: Wait until the APU flap is closed — about **2 min** after the APU AVAIL light goes out — or smoke may enter the cabin on the next flight. With batteries off and the APU running, APU fire extinguishing is unavailable.

items.detail: This checklist is read-and-do.

phases.title: Rejected Takeoff
phases.note: Below 100 kt: reject for any ECAM warning or caution or another significant failure — captain's decision. Between 100 kt and V1 be **go-minded** and reject only for the cases below. After V1: continue.

items.sub: REJECT BETWEEN 100 kt AND V1 ONLY FOR

items.detail: Malfunctions or conditions that give unambiguous indications that the aircraft will not fly safely.
Any red warning. During the takeoff inhibit only a few alerts can appear at all — see the list at the bottom.

items.item: Amber: ENG FAIL · REV · THR LVR · SIDESTICK
items.detail: Only these amber cautions: ENG 1(2) FAIL, ENG 1(2) REVERSER FAULT or REVERSE UNLOCKED, ENG 1(2) THR LEVER FAULT, F/CTL SIDESTICK FAULT.
Only with significant airspeed variations below V1 and enough runway left to stop.

items.item: Tire Failure within 20 kt of V1
items.detail: Unless debris causes noticeable engine parameter fluctuation: take off, reduce fuel load and land with full runway length available.

items.caution: Autobrake only becomes active **above 72 kt**. Below that the blue ON light stays lit but the autobrake is **not braking** — use manual brakes with maximum force.

items.detail: Go to the Ground Emergency / Emergency Evacuation checklist whenever the situation threatens passengers and crew.

From the malfunction occurring to brakes and spoilers working fully, about 5 seconds pass. Rejecting 4 kt after V1 with no stop margin can mean a runway overrun at up to 70 kt groundspeed. Statistically about half of all unsuccessful rejected takeoffs could have been avoided by continuing; roughly a quarter of those were tire failures.

items.state: FIRE · OIL LO PR · DUAL FAIL
items.detail: ENG 1(2) FIRE, ENG 1(2) OIL LO PR, ENG DUAL FAILURE, APU FIRE, F/CTL L+R ELEV FAULT, CONFIG WARNING.

ENG 1(2) FAIL, ENG 1(2) SHUTDOWN, ENG 1(2) REV UNLOCKED, ENG 1(2) THR LEVER FAULT, F/CTL L(R) SIDESTICK FAULT, FWS FWC 1+2 FAULT. The T.O. inhibit phase runs from the first engine reaching takeoff power until 1500 ft AGL or 2 min after takeoff.

phases.title: Engine Failure after V1
phases.note: Continue the takeoff. **No action below 400 ft AGL** except silencing aural warnings and gear up.

items.detail: Then follow SRS. The simulator sheet gives 10–13°.
Centre the blue beta target with the rudder pedals, then take the pressure off with rudder trim.

items.caution: TOGA: **10 min** with one engine inoperative, 5 min with all engines (CFM56-5B).
items.detail: The maximum engine-out acceleration altitude in the takeoff performance is based on this limit.
ECAM procedure is applied once an appropriate flight path is established and the aircraft is at least 400 ft AGL.
With no AP or FD available, limit bank angle to 15° until reaching F, S or green dot speed.

items.caution: Level off once the engine is secured — at the latest at the maximum acceleration altitude (TOGA time limit).
items.detail: Push to level off (or V/S 0), let the speed increase and retract the flaps on schedule. An engine fire is secured with the agent discharged; a failure without damage with the master switch OFF.
Follow EO routing, radar vectors, or an immediate turn back.

phases.title: Engine Out — Quick VMC Return
phases.note: Visual circuit back to the departure runway with one engine out. Timing on downwind: **45 s ± 1 s per kt** of wind component.

items.detail: This is an alternative quick-return configuration strategy at acceleration altitude. Do not first clean up to CONF 0 and then follow a sequence that assumes CONF 1.
45 seconds, adjusted by 1 second per knot of wind component.

phases.title: Go-Around
phases.note: TOGA engages the go-around phase. If TOGA thrust is not needed, the levers can be retarded after briefly passing through the detent — CL keeps the benefit of A/THR.

items.detail: Then follow FD SRS.

items.caution: FULL → 3 · 3 → 2. There is **no stopping at flaps 2** during the later clean-up.

items.detail: MAN TOGA · SRS · GA TRK · A/THR in blue.
Minimum 100 ft before changing lateral mode.
A go-around can be flown with both autopilots; engaging any other mode disengages AP2.
If speed does not increase, check and pull the ALT knob.
Divert: enable the alternate. Second approach: activate the approach phase.

items.sub: DISCONTINUED APPROACH — AT OR ABOVE FCU ALT

items.detail: An alternative to a full go-around when at or above the FCU selected altitude. Below it, go around.

items.caution: Since the levers never reach TOGA, the FMS stays in approach phase. Overflying the airport sequences the destination — a lateral revision will be needed to redefine it.

phases.title: Emergency Descent
phases.note: Memory items first, followed by the applicable ECAM/QRH procedure. The old descent-rate, time and distance figures are source examples, not guaranteed descent performance.

items.caution: At high flight levels, monitor VLS while extending the speed brakes — angle-of-attack protection can retract them and disconnect the AP.

items.detail: If structural damage is suspected (loud bang, high cabin vertical speed): set SPEED/MACH to SPEED to prevent an IAS increase, and use the speed brakes carefully.
The supplied QRH uses “consider”; squawk 7700 unless otherwise specified by ATC. Preserve the condition instead of turning it into an unconditional action.
The MORA displayed on the ND is the highest MORA value within 40 NM of the aircraft.
Press MASK MAN ON. It may be pressed before reaching 14 000 ft once it is obvious the cabin altitude will exceed it.

phases.title: Circling Approach
phases.note: Minima are the higher of the published chart values or **MDH 600 ft AGL / visibility 2400 m**. Use TRK-FPA throughout; keep AP and A/THR until the final descent.

items.caution: Once SEC F-PLN is activated the go-around is tied to the landing runway, not the instrument approach. If visual reference is lost, go around using selected guidance and fly the **original** missed approach.

items.detail: Also insert it as a constraint at the final descent point.
Proceed to downwind; 30 s once wings are level after the turn.

items.caution: Do not descend before the runway threshold is identified and you are on the correct descent path.

items.detail: Ensure early stabilisation.

phases.title: Visual Approach
phases.note: Accept a visual approach **only** if: visibility over 5 km · positive ground contact · cloud base at least 2000 ft above · preceding traffic in sight · daytime.

items.detail: Selected for reference — but fly on visual references.
Use the wind vector on the ND so the downwind track sits about 2.5–3 NM out — the inner range circle margin.
Before turning base.

phases.title: Touch and Go
phases.note: Training manoeuvre. After touchdown the critical sequence is flaps 2, N1 50%, trim in the green band, **then** TOGA.

items.caution: Do not select TOGA before the pitch trim is back in the green band.

items.detail: Thrust roughly equal to gross weight in tonnes.
Reduce thrust to about 45%, then slowly to F speed.
Speed at F.

phases.title: Overweight Landing
phases.note: Overweight landing requires aircraft-specific performance and the applicable abnormal procedure. This source-derived card is a study reference until those requirements are confirmed.

items.caution: No verified overweight table for the CFM sharklet aircraft is available.
items.detail: Use the landing performance of the Fenix EFB for the actual mass, configuration and conditions.
Packs off (or on APU) increases maximum available engine thrust in the event of a go-around.
Reduce the FCU selected speed to reach VLS at the runway threshold.
Maximum braking may be used after nosewheel touchdown. If landing distance permits, delay or reduce braking to use the full runway.

items.caution: Be prepared for tyre deflation if brake temperature exceeds **800 °C**.

phases.title: Crossbleed Engine Start
phases.note: Used to start the second engine from the running engine's bleed air.

items.caution: This procedure should only be performed with the **parking brake set**.

items.detail: Behind and in front of the engine.

items.caution: Obtain 30 PSI bleed pressure before start initiation and maintain at least **25 PSI** throughout the start.

phases.title: Engine Start — External Air
phases.note: Engine start with an external air cart when the APU cannot supply bleed air: engine 2 from the cart, engine 1 from the cart as well or by crossbleed.

items.detail: Prevents pack contamination.
Minimum recommended starter air supply pressure is 30 PSI with the starter valve open.

items.sub: IF EXTERNAL AIR ALSO STARTS ENGINE 1

phases.title: Low Visibility T/O & Turbulence
phases.note: Low-visibility takeoff (LVP, RVR below 400 m) and flying through severe turbulence.

items.detail: Whichever is higher.
Payload permitting.
Localizer, ND, runway markings.
So emergency services can identify the aircraft.

items.caution: Wait for target speed +20 kt (limited to VFE−5) before retracting slats or flaps.

items.detail: Set thrust to turbulence N1 from the QRH.
To keep the benefit of ground-speed mini.
CONF FULL gives better handling in turbulence; CONF 3 gives more energy and less drag.
250 kt up to FL200, 275 kt or M0.76 above FL200.

phases.title: QFE Operations
phases.note: Mainly Russian and CIS airspace. Rule of thumb: **1 hPa ≈ 27 ft**. QNH = QFE + (threshold elevation ÷ 27).

items.detail: With QFE set, the altimeter reads 0 ft on the airfield (height above the field). With QNH set, it reads elevation above mean sea level.
The same FL system in feet applies at or above transition altitude/height/level.
Example UUWW RWY 01, threshold 630 ft: 630 ÷ 27 = 23 hPa. Reported QFE 997 → QNH = 997 + 23 = 1020 hPa. Altimeters then read 630 ft on the ground.
Departure chart example: initial climb 900 m QFE = 3640 ft QNH → set 3700 ft on the FCU. A later clearance to 1200 m QFE = 4630 ft.
Leaving QFE on the standby instrument gives a direct height reference while the PFDs run on QNH.

items.caution: The metre indication on the SD page uses a simple feet-to-metres conversion — treat it as advisory.

items.detail: With QFE selected on the FCU, altitude values entered are QFE feet: 600 m QFE ≈ 2000 ft QFE (1977 ft exactly).

phases.title: G/S Interception from Above
phases.note: Only when cleared for the approach, established on the localizer and with enough distance to be stabilised by 1000 ft. Otherwise ask for vectors or go around.

items.caution: With the FCU altitude below the aircraft, ALT* would engage before the glide slope is captured.

items.detail: Monitor the speed; do not let it run away from the configuration you need.
Landing gear and flaps 2 give the best rate of descent. Respect VFE; speed brakes are not recommended below 2000 ft.

phases.title: Hot & High Airports
phases.note: Cusco, La Paz, Quito, Bogotá, Paro, Mexico City, Addis Ababa: high elevation and heat mean high true airspeed, long distances and less thrust. Performance only from the Fenix EFB with actual temperature, QNH and wind.

items.detail: Expect TOGA or a small FLEX margin. Check the engine-out acceleration altitude and the climb gradient against terrain.

items.state: OFF or APU BLEED IF REQUIRED
items.detail: Improves takeoff performance when the EFB needs it.
High true airspeed plus tailwind can reach the tire limit at rotation.
Thin air means slower light-up and higher EGT — monitor the auto-start closely.
VAPP stays an indicated speed; the ground speed is much higher. Longer landing distance and more brake energy.
The cabin is scheduled to the airport elevation automatically; after landing the cabin altitude equals the high field elevation.

phases.title: Short Runway
phases.note: Funafuti, St Helena, Skiathos: plan the stop before you plan the approach. Landing distance from the EFB with the actual runway condition, then keep your margin. Your world tour has test legs for Funafuti and St Helena.

items.detail: Lowest approach speed; CONF 3 only if the performance allows it.
LO is for long runways.
The FMGS already adds the wind correction; every extra knot adds landing distance.
A long flare or float is a go-around, not a correction to force onto the runway.

phases.title: Cold Weather & Contaminated Runway
phases.note: Union Glacier and winter stops: treat blue ice and snow as contaminated — performance from the EFB with the correct runway condition, a reduced crosswind limit and gentle inputs. Union Glacier is a test leg of your world tour.

items.detail: Engine run-ups at intervals during long taxi in freezing fog or precipitation.
With slush or snow keep the flaps up until the holding point.
Contaminated runways have lower crosswind limits — use the value for the reported runway condition.
After an approach in icing or on a contaminated runway, retract only once the ground crew has checked for ice.

phases.title: BEFORE START
phases.note: Read after the cockpit preparation flow is complete. The flow does the work — the checklist catches omissions.

items.detail: Checks: auto brake MAX · signs on · spoilers armed · flaps set to T/O · TO config normal.
Checks: landing gear down · signs on · spoilers armed · flaps set to landing config.

phases.title: AFTER LANDING
phases.note: Silent checklist in many operators. Consider adverse weather before retracting the flaps.

phases.title: SECURING
phases.note: Read-and-do checklist. Apply when the last passenger has left and the aircraft will be unattended.

changes.title: V2-Korrekturen übernommen
changes.text: Getrennte FCU-Freigabehöhe, THR RED/ACC nach Abflugverfahren, kein Ersatz-CG, Fahrwerk pro Bein, Fuel-Check am gleichen Punkt, Engine-out ohne Widerspruch, 7700 mit Bedingung, Touch-and-go-Reihenfolge.

changes.title: Konkrete Werte zurück
changes.text: Wo V2 korrekte Zahlen durch „as briefed“ ersetzt hat, stehen sie wieder da – mit Quelle: Taxi 30 → 10 kt (FCTM), AP-Mindesthöhen 100/160/250 ft, TOGA 5/10 min, Öl 9,5 qt + 0,5 qt/h.

changes.title: After Takeoff / Climb
changes.text: V1 behauptete, die Checkliste gebe es nicht mehr; V2 räumte ein, dass es sie gibt, ließ sie aber weg. Sie ist jetzt da und im Flow eingehängt.

changes.title: Startabbruch nach Airbus
changes.text: Zwischen 100 kt und V1 nicht mehr „jede ECAM-Meldung“, sondern Feuer, schwere Schäden, Schubverlust, Flugunfähigkeit, rote Warnungen und fünf bestimmte Amber-Cautions.

changes.title: Anflug ohne Widersprüche
changes.text: Wing Anti-Ice bei sichtbarem Eisansatz statt „nur bei starker Vereisung“; Stabilisierung 1000 ft (500 ft visuell); die 1500 ft der Quelle als Betreiberwert markiert.

changes.title: Drei Anflugarten
changes.text: Der Normal-Flow kennt jetzt ILS, RNAV mit FINAL APP und Nichtpräzisionsanflüge mit TRK/FPA – umgeschaltet im Flugprofil, mit CDFA-Hinweis und Kodierungsprüfung.

changes.title: Vier neue Karten
changes.text: G/S von oben, Hot & High (Cusco, La Paz, Quito …), kurze Bahnen (Funafuti, St Helena …) sowie Kälte und kontaminierte Bahn (Union Glacier).

changes.title: Eurowings und IAE entfernt
changes.text: Flottenseite, Streckenkarte, Pack-Flow-Bezug und IAE-Leerlaufwerte sind raus; V3 ist auf den Fenix A320 CEO mit CFM56-5B und Sharklets ausgelegt.

changes.title: Im Look der Weltreise
changes.text: Gleiche Farben, Schriften und Bausteine wie die Weltreise V2: Phasen-Leiste über den ganzen Flug, Briefing links, Schritte und Profil rechts, Tracks und Reiter.

changes.title: Eine Datenquelle
changes.text: Alle Inhalte stehen in flow-v3.json und werden per build_v3.py zur Offline-Datei. Die stabilen Schritt-IDs aus V2 bleiben – Häkchen überleben Änderungen.
